headline.headline: THEODORE ENDS IT IN DOUBLE OT AS GOLDEN KNIGHTS GRAB 2-1 SERIES LEAD OVER HURRICANES
headline.deck: Vegas defenseman's overtime winner caps wild four-goal comeback in Game 3
headline.body:
LAS VEGAS — Shea Theodore scored in double overtime Saturday night to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 5-4 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 3, a stunning reversal that puts Vegas in command of the series at two games to one. The Golden Knights clawed back from a 4-0 deficit, scoring four straight goals before Theodore delivered the series-turning blow in the second extra period.

The Hurricanes, who had stunned Vegas with four consecutive goals to seize what appeared to be a comfortable lead, could not hold on as the Golden Knights surged back in a game that produced eight total goals and played deep into the night. Carolina's collapse in the second period, allowing four straight, will be the defining sequence for a team that now faces an uphill road in the series.

For the Golden Knights, the victory resonates far beyond one game. Vegas has now won back-to-back after dropping the opener, and with Theodore emerging as a hero from the blue line, the Golden Knights have positioned themselves within two wins of the Stanley Cup Finals. The Hurricanes, deflated and facing a 2-1 deficit, return home for Game 4 needing a response or risk watching the series slip away entirely.

secondary.headline: KNICKS BRING 2-0 EDGE HOME TO GARDEN FOR GAME 3 — WITH TRUMP IN THE CROWD
secondary.deck: New York warns fans of heightened security as high-profile guest expected Sunday night
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Knicks carry a commanding 2-0 series lead over the San Antonio Spurs into Madison Square Garden for Game 3 Sunday night, but the biggest pregame storyline may be off the court. The Knicks organization has warned fans to bring as little as possible to the arena, citing stepped-up security measures tied to the expected attendance of former President Donald Trump.

On the floor, New York has handled the Spurs — who finished the regular season at 62-20 and entered as the conference's most formidable team — with surprising authority through two games. San Antonio, playing without home-court advantage for the first time in this postseason, now faces the deafening noise of a sold-out Garden crowd and a New York team surging with confidence.

secondary.headline: CUBS WALK OFF IN TEN AS CROW-ARMSTRONG PACES CHICAGO PAST GIANTS
secondary.deck: Chicago wins 3-2 in extras behind Pete Crow-Armstrong's four-hit effort
secondary.body:
CHICAGO — Pete Crow-Armstrong carried the Chicago Cubs on his back Saturday, collecting four hits and fueling a 3-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants in ten innings at Wrigley Field before an announced crowd of 39,248. The game was tied at one after six innings and again at two after nine before Chicago pushed across the winning run in the bottom of the tenth.

Matt Amaya was hit by a pitch from Erik Miller during the contest, per official game notes, and the Giants managed to knot the score with a run in the ninth before the Cubs answered in the tenth to seal the win. Chicago, now 34-31 and fourth in the NL Central, relied on Crow-Armstrong's bat to pull away from a Giants club sitting at 26-39 and struggling to find consistency on the road.

secondary.headline: ROYALS RALLY IN NINTH TO STUN TWINS, 3-2
secondary.deck: Kansas City scores twice in the final frame to escape Minnesota with a road win
secondary.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — The Kansas City Royals were clinging to a one-run deficit entering the ninth inning Saturday when they erupted for two runs to stun the Minnesota Twins 3-2 before 20,555 at Target Field. Kansas City had led 1-0 after the first inning but watched Minnesota answer with runs in the fifth and eighth to take a late edge, only to see the Royals respond with a decisive two-run burst in the ninth.

Victor Caratini was hit by a pitch from Alex Lange during the game, per official notes, and the Royals got key contributions throughout the lineup to manufacture the comeback. The result denied the Twins a series win and kept Kansas City in contention in a tight American League Central race.

column.headline: CAROLINA SQUANDERED SOMETHING SPECIAL — AND VEGAS WON'T FORGET IT
column.body:
Four goals. Carolina had a four-goal lead against one of the most dangerous teams in hockey, on the road no less, and could not hold it. That is not bad luck. That is a failure of will, structure, and composure at the worst possible moment. The Hurricanes now trail 2-1 in a series they looked to be controlling, and the ghosts of that second period will follow them back to Raleigh.

Shea Theodore scoring in double overtime is the kind of moment franchises build mythology around. The Golden Knights have done this before — absorb a punch, absorb another, then throw one that ends the night. Carolina knows the formula now. The question is whether they have the resolve to answer it, because in a best-of-seven, allowing a team to believe they cannot be beaten is the most dangerous gift a team can give an opponent.

story.headline: ASTROS POUND ATHLETICS 13-2, ALVAREZ BLASTS NO. 22 IN FIVE-INNING ROUT
story.deck: Houston erupts for six runs in the fifth to blow open a lopsided Saturday night affair.
story.body:
HOUSTON — Yordan Alvarez crushed his 22nd home run of the season and the Astros turned a competitive game into a laugher with a six-run fifth inning Saturday, rolling past the Athletics 13-2 at Minute Maid Park before 30,211 fans. Houston had already staked a 6-2 lead through three innings, but the fifth-inning outburst — the largest single-inning explosion on any diamond Saturday — ended any doubt and sent the Oakland bench home early.

Jose Altuve added his fifth home run of the year and a player identified in the scorebook only as Jr. chipped in a solo shot as well, his first of the campaign. Nestor Cortes earned the victory and also was charged with a wild pitch. Houston finished with extra-base hits from Martin Peña, Christian Walker, Isaac Paredes, Jr. and Jose Vázquez, a two-double barrage that kept the Athletics' pitching staff scrambling all night. The A's stranded 18 baserunners, a futile accumulation that underscored their inability to answer Houston's firepower.

Elsewhere Saturday, the Chicago Cubs edged the San Francisco Giants 3-2 in ten innings at Wrigley Field, with Pete Crow-Armstrong providing the decisive blow — his 11th home run — before 39,248. The St. Louis Cardinals outlasted the Cincinnati Reds 6-5 on Lars Nootbaar's home run and Jordan Walker's 16th of the year, with St. Louis leaving 22 runners on base in a chaotic night at Busch Stadium. The Seattle Mariners blanked the Detroit Tigers 4-0 behind Dominic Canzone's eighth homer, keeping Seattle atop the AL West at 34-31.

story.headline: KNICKS HOLD COMMANDING 2-0 GRIP ON SPURS AS FINALS SHIFT TO MADISON SQUARE GARDEN
story.deck: New York enters Game 3 as heavy favorites with San Antonio desperately needing a turnaround.
story.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Knicks have seized control of the 2026 NBA Finals, taking a 2-0 series lead over the San Antonio Spurs and returning home to Madison Square Garden where the city is ready to erupt. The third-seeded Knicks, who finished the regular season 53-29, have stunned the 62-win Spurs through two games in San Antonio, silencing a roster that was widely considered the most complete team in basketball heading into the postseason. Oddsmakers have since installed New York as commanding championship favorites, a seismic shift from before the series tipped off.

Game 3 on Sunday carries an added layer of spectacle and security. President Donald Trump is expected to attend at Madison Square Garden, prompting the Knicks organization to issue a formal warning to fans, urging ticket holders to bring as little as possible to the arena and arrive early to account for enhanced screening procedures. The combination of Finals basketball and a presidential visit is expected to make the Garden experience unlike anything fans have encountered in recent memory.

Meanwhile, the broader NBA Finals conversation includes lessons from Game 2 that Spurs head coach Gregg Popovich and his staff must address before tipoff Sunday. San Antonio's half-court offense stalled in critical fourth-quarter possessions, and the Knicks' physical perimeter defense repeatedly disrupted the Spurs' ball movement. Adding to the league's festive atmosphere, Taylor Swift's courtside seat from the Eastern Conference Finals — the one she shared with fiancé Travis Kelce during Game 3 against Cleveland — has surfaced in a public bidding frenzy, underscoring just how deeply NBA playoff fever has gripped the entire country this June.

story.headline: THEODORE'S 2OT WINNER PUTS GOLDEN KNIGHTS ON STANLEY CUP DOORSTEP
story.deck: Vegas rallies from 4-0 deficit to stun Carolina in double overtime, leads series 2-1
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — Defenseman Shea Theodore scored in double overtime Saturday night to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 5-4 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, a wild and careening contest that saw four straight goals from each club before Theodore finally ended it and handed Vegas a commanding 2-1 series lead.

The Hurricanes had stormed out to a 4-0 lead before the Golden Knights authored one of the most stunning reversals in recent Stanley Cup Final history, scoring four consecutive goals to force a tie. Carolina clawed back to knot the game in the third period, sending the contest to overtime, but Vegas would not be denied. Theodore's decisive goal in the second extra period extinguished whatever momentum the Hurricanes had manufactured in front of a stunned road crowd.

Carolina now faces a 2-1 series deficit and must reckon with how a four-goal cushion evaporated entirely in a single game. The Hurricanes allowed four goals in the second period, briefly appeared to have salvaged a critical road point with a third-period equalizer, then watched it slip away across 80-plus minutes of desperate hockey. Game 4 is scheduled for Monday, and the Hurricanes must win or face elimination pressure with the series returning to Vegas.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are betting big on new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into one of the most turbulent quarterback markets in recent memory, with multiple franchises overhauling their rosters just months after the Los Angeles Rams captured Super Bowl LX in February. The Cleveland Browns made the boldest move of the spring, agreeing to a four-year, $192 million deal with free agent quarterback Sam Darnold, banking on his rejuvenated play to finally stabilize a position that has plagued the franchise for decades. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders pulled off a stunning trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, acquiring Justin Fields in exchange for two first-round picks and a package of young defensive talent.

The 2026 NFL Draft in late April produced its share of intrigue as well. The Tennessee Titans, selecting second overall, drafted Oregon quarterback Dante Carver, a 6-foot-4 dual-threat prospect widely regarded as the crown jewel of a deep quarterback class. Draft analysts praised Titans general manager ran Carthon for surrounding Carver with a rebuilt offensive line, having already signed veteran guard Isaac Seumalo in early free agency to anchor the interior. The New York Giants, picking fifth, surprised the league by trading back three spots with the New England Patriots, accumulating additional capital before ultimately selecting Georgia edge rusher Marcus Holloway.

Training camp storylines are already taking shape across the league. In Green Bay, Jordan Love enters his third full season as the Packers starter under heightened expectations after a disappointing 2025 campaign ended in a first-round playoff exit. Head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged this week that the offense will install a more aggressive downfield passing scheme designed to unlock Love's arm strength. In Dallas, the Cowboys continue to navigate uncertainty at multiple skill positions after releasing wide receiver CeeDee Lamb in a cost-cutting move that stunned the football world back in March, a decision owner Jerry Jones defended as necessary to remain competitive under the tightening salary cap.
